Phalaenopsis ( / ˌ f æ l ɪ ˈ n ɒ p s ɪ s / ), also known as moth orchids , [ 2 ] is a genus of about seventy species of plants in the family Orchidaceae . Orchids in this genus are monopodial epiphytes or lithophytes with long, coarse roots, short, leafy stems and long-lasting, flat flowers arranged in a flowering stem that often branches near the end. Orchids in this genus are native to Asia, New Guinea , and Australia, but mostly occur in Indonesia and the Philippines .
